lines.say: Stop tapping 'update payment' in that AI bill email. Open the app.
lines.show: Stop tapping that email. Open the app.
lines.visual: Frame 0: title 'STOP TAPPING THAT EMAIL' at 120 px or more above y 560, with 'EMAIL' in Playfair Italic in the accent. Beside the host, a phone mock-up on a hostel desk shows a red 'Payment failed' banner. A small amber 'EXAMPLE' tag sits on the phone. This is our own mock screen, not a real email.

lines.say: Payment failed. Update in two days.
lines.visual: Full email card, our own mock, labelled EXAMPLE: sender row, subject 'Payment failed', body 'Update within 48 hours', and a red 'Update payment' button. A 48-hour timer ring ticks down in amber.

lines.say: India's free year of the Go plan started a year ago, so people are checking renewals.
lines.show: Free Go year opened Nov 2025. Renewals now.
lines.visual: A calendar chip 'Nov 2025' pops beside the email card, and a small 'Renewal?' amber chip wobbles. The email card stays on screen, full.

lines.say: Reports show the link leads to a photocopied shop counter.
lines.show: The link opens a photocopied counter.
lines.visual: Diagram 1, full width: two shop counters side by side with the same signboard ('ChatGPT') and the same login form. The real one has a green 'REAL' tag and the copy has a red 'COPY' tag. They build in order: the counters, then the signboards, then the forms, then the tags. Small 'Source: reports' label.

lines.say: Same shop name. The address has one wrong letter.
lines.visual: Diagram 2: an address-bar strip types out a look-alike address, our own EXAMPLE and not a real scam domain. It types letter by letter, then one letter turns red and a red ring draws around it. A buzz plays on 'wrong'.

lines.say: Your password and OTP drop into a stranger's drawer.
lines.show: Your OTP lands in a stranger's drawer.
lines.visual: Diagram 3: the copy counter's form fills with dots for the password and a 6-box OTP. A red arrow draws itself from the form down into an open drawer labelled 'stranger'. The OTP chip drops in, and the drawer slides shut with a click.

lines.say: Open the app yourself: Settings, then Subscription.
lines.show: Open the app: Settings, then Subscription.
lines.card: Check billing only inside the app: Settings, then Subscription. Never from an email link.
lines.visual: Payoff, full rule card titled 'The real counter' with 'app' in Playfair Italic in the accent. Three rows tick green on the beat: 1 Open the app yourself, 2 Settings, 3 Subscription. A red strike draws across a small 'email link' chip at the bottom.

lines.say: The catch: careful fakes look perfect. Always open the app.
lines.show: The catch: fakes can look perfect.
lines.visual: The two counters return small and identical, and an amber 'Address check: not enough' chip appears. A green 'Open the app yourself' chip pops below it as the answer.
A helpline card with '1930' large in ink and 'cybercrime.gov.in' below it as plain text, not a link. A pop plays as the number lands.

lines.say: Send this to the friend who took the free AI year. Comment SAFE.
lines.show: Send this. Comment SAFE for the card.
lines.visual: End card: 'Save.' in the serif with a bookmark shape, a quiet dark pill 'Comment SAFE', and a small sticker 'FREE · Family AI Safety Card'.

preflight: Confirm the SAFE keyword has a live Family AI Safety Card on the tools page and in docs/EXPLAINER.md before posting. If it is missing, add the tool or answer SAFE DMs by hand.
Every email, address and OTP on screen is our own mock and is labelled EXAMPLE. No real victim, no real scam domain.
Claims from secondary sources (GBlock, Cofense summary) are worded as 'reports show', with no statistics. Say nothing about what happens when the free Go year ends.
